items.author: astralwave
items.text:
Oh yes, I know! I tried to use Dots to steer Codex and it was a nightmare. 

I ended up having to setup a custom tunnel MCP so my Dot can tunnel into my Mac and drive agents via the Paseo MCP. It works better than its native Codex orchestration, but still wasn’t great (it doesn’t know how to prompt agents! It talks to external agents like its own internal thinking trace and as if those agents share its context window), so I stopped doing that.

Grok Bot is better but it eats tokens like crazy. Still figuring out my setup there but it at least reliably reacts to a Tibo reset and then burns it down to 0 as quickly as possible before the next reset. 

The best coordinator setup I found so far is Claude Projects. Lot of rough edges now since it’s beta (especially around permissions), but I feel the most productive in it. 

Especially when you lean into using Artifacts to review work and make decisions.

zh-CN.title: 用 Dots、Grok Bot 和 Claude Projects 协调编程 Agent 的体验
zh-CN.summary: 作者试过让 Dots 指挥 Codex，体验很差，后来自建隧道 MCP 让 Dot 连进 Mac、通过 Paseo MCP 驱动 Agent，比原生编排好但仍不理想，因为它不会给外部 Agent 写提示。Grok Bot 更好但很耗 token。目前他觉得最好的协调方案是 Claude Projects，测试版问题不少（尤其权限）。

zh-TW.title: 用 Dots、Grok Bot 和 Claude Projects 協調程式 Agent 的體驗
zh-TW.summary: 作者試過讓 Dots 指揮 Codex，體驗很差，後來自建隧道 MCP 讓 Dot 連進 Mac、透過 Paseo MCP 驅動 Agent，比原生編排好但仍不理想，因為它不會給外部 Agent 寫提示。Grok Bot 更好但很耗 token。目前他覺得最好的協調方案是 Claude Projects，測試版問題不少（尤其權限）。

en.title: Coordinating coding agents with Dots, Grok Bot and Claude Projects
en.summary: The author tried having Dots steer Codex and called it a nightmare; a custom tunnel MCP letting the Dot drive agents on his Mac via the Paseo MCP worked better than native orchestration but still poorly, because it doesn’t know how to prompt other agents. Grok Bot is better but eats tokens. His best coordinator so far is Claude Projects, still rough in beta, especially permissions.

ja.title: Dots、Grok Bot、Claude Projectsでコーディングエージェントを指揮した感想
ja.summary: 作者はDotsでCodexを動かそうとして散々だった。独自のトンネルMCPでDotをMacにつなぎPaseo MCP経由でエージェントを動かすと標準の連携よりましだが、外部エージェントへの指示の出し方が下手でやめた。Grok Botは良いがトークン消費が激しい。今のところ最良はClaude Projectsだが、ベータで権限まわりに粗さがある。

ko.title: Dots, Grok Bot, Claude Projects로 코딩 에이전트 조율해 본 경험
ko.summary: 작성자는 Dots로 Codex를 조종하려다 악몽을 겪었다. 자체 터널 MCP로 Dot이 Mac에서 Paseo MCP를 통해 에이전트를 움직이게 하니 기본 기능보다 나았지만, 외부 에이전트에 프롬프트를 잘 못 줘서 그만뒀다. Grok Bot은 더 낫지만 토큰을 많이 먹는다. 지금까지 최고의 조율 도구는 Claude Projects지만 베타라 권한 쪽이 거칠다.

ms.title: Menyelaras ejen pengekodan dengan Dots, Grok Bot dan Claude Projects
ms.summary: Penulis cuba menggunakan Dots untuk mengemudi Codex dan menyifatkannya mimpi ngeri; MCP terowong sendiri yang membolehkan Dot memacu ejen di Mac melalui Paseo MCP lebih baik daripada orkestrasi asal tetapi masih lemah kerana ia tidak tahu memberi prompt kepada ejen lain. Grok Bot lebih baik tetapi banyak makan token. Penyelaras terbaiknya setakat ini ialah Claude Projects, masih kasar dalam beta terutama kebenaran.

vi.title: Điều phối agent lập trình bằng Dots, Grok Bot và Claude Projects
vi.summary: Tác giả thử dùng Dots điều khiển Codex và gọi đó là ác mộng; một MCP đường hầm tự dựng cho Dot điều khiển agent trên Mac qua Paseo MCP tốt hơn cơ chế gốc nhưng vẫn kém, vì nó không biết cách viết prompt cho agent khác. Grok Bot tốt hơn nhưng tốn token. Bộ điều phối tốt nhất anh thấy là Claude Projects, còn thô ở bản beta, nhất là phần quyền.

fr.title: Coordonner des agents de code avec Dots, Grok Bot et Claude Projects
fr.summary: L’auteur a essayé de piloter Codex avec Dots, un cauchemar ; un MCP tunnel maison permettant au Dot de piloter des agents sur son Mac via le MCP Paseo marchait mieux que l’orchestration native, mais mal, faute de savoir rédiger des prompts pour d’autres agents. Grok Bot est meilleur mais très gourmand en jetons. Son meilleur coordinateur : Claude Projects, encore brut en bêta, surtout côté permissions.

es.title: Coordinar agentes de código con Dots, Grok Bot y Claude Projects
es.summary: El autor probó a dirigir Codex con Dots y fue una pesadilla; un MCP de túnel propio para que el Dot manejara agentes en su Mac vía el MCP de Paseo funcionó mejor que la orquestación nativa, pero mal, porque no sabe darles prompts a otros agentes. Grok Bot es mejor pero gasta muchos tokens. Su mejor coordinador por ahora es Claude Projects, aún tosco en beta, sobre todo en permisos.

de.title: Coding-Agents mit Dots, Grok Bot und Claude Projects koordinieren
de.summary: Der Autor ließ Dots Codex steuern, ein Albtraum; ein eigenes Tunnel-MCP, mit dem der Dot über das Paseo-MCP Agents auf seinem Mac steuert, lief besser als die native Orchestrierung, aber schwach, weil er anderen Agents keine guten Prompts gibt. Grok Bot ist besser, frisst aber Tokens. Sein bester Koordinator bisher: Claude Projects, in der Beta noch holprig, vor allem bei Berechtigungen.

items.author: tomcohen
items.text:
I mostly felt that way too, but over the last couple of days something that helped me a lot is trying to think "how do I manage an employee" when thinking about Dot. When I was a manager it would never have worked if I just tried to track everything in a single DM inbox with each of my engineers, so I just shouldn't try to do the same thing with Dot.
If Dot was another person that I was working with on a bunch of things, I'd try to use tools like task managers (e.g. todoist) and knowledge bases (e.g. notion) to keep track of what they're up to, what they did, what they delivered, what's still open, what needs my attention, etc. We'd dm each other when we need to, but we wouldn't try to make this the only way we'd organise stuff. 
So I've started doing the same thing with Elminster (my Dot), and so far it seems to work pretty well. We have a notion workspace where Elminster documents where things are on different projects, their next steps, blockers, decisions needed from me, etc. As unfathomably corporate brain as it sounds I have daily 1:1s with him to get an overview of where things stand and what's next.
It's VERY far from perfect, but it works *much* better than it did when I just tried to talk to him to the Dots single chat. Really recommend people to try this reframe and see what you think.

zh-CN.title: 像管理员工一样管理你的 Dot
zh-CN.summary: 作者发现只在 Dots 单一对话里沟通效果差，于是像管理工程师那样对待自己的 Dot（名叫 Elminster）：在 Notion 工作区里让它记录各项目进度、下一步、阻碍和需要他决定的事，并每天和它做 1:1 了解进展。他说远不完美，但比只聊天好得多。

zh-TW.title: 像管理員工一樣管理你的 Dot
zh-TW.summary: 作者發現只在 Dots 單一對話裡溝通效果差，於是像管理工程師那樣對待自己的 Dot（名叫 Elminster）：在 Notion 工作區裡讓它記錄各專案進度、下一步、阻礙和需要他決定的事，並每天和它做 1:1 了解進展。他說遠不完美，但比只聊天好得多。

en.title: Manage your Dot like an employee
en.summary: Tracking everything in the single Dots chat didn’t work, so the author treats his Dot, Elminster, like an engineer he manages: Elminster documents project status, next steps, blockers and decisions needed in a Notion workspace, and they hold daily 1:1s. He says it’s far from perfect but works much better than chat alone.

ja.title: Dotを部下のようにマネジメントする
ja.summary: Dotsの単一チャットだけで管理するのはうまくいかなかったため、作者は自分のDot「Elminster」を部下のエンジニアのように扱う。Notionのワークスペースに各プロジェクトの状況、次の手順、障害、判断が必要な事項を記録させ、毎日1対1で状況を確認する。完璧には程遠いが、チャットだけよりずっと良いという。

ko.title: Dot을 직원처럼 관리하기
ko.summary: Dots 단일 채팅에서 모든 걸 관리하니 잘 안 돼서, 작성자는 자기 Dot인 Elminster를 관리하는 엔지니어처럼 대한다. Notion 워크스페이스에 프로젝트 현황, 다음 단계, 장애 요소, 결정이 필요한 사항을 기록하게 하고 매일 1:1을 한다. 완벽과는 거리가 멀지만 채팅만 할 때보다 훨씬 낫다고 한다.

ms.title: Urus Dot anda seperti pekerja
ms.summary: Menjejak segalanya dalam satu sembang Dots tidak berkesan, jadi penulis melayan Dot-nya, Elminster, seperti jurutera yang diurusnya: Elminster mendokumenkan status projek, langkah seterusnya, halangan dan keputusan yang perlu dalam ruang kerja Notion, dan mereka mengadakan 1:1 harian. Katanya jauh dari sempurna tetapi jauh lebih baik daripada sembang sahaja.

Anh nói còn xa mới hoàn hảo nhưng tốt hơn nhiều so với chỉ chat.

fr.title: Gérer son Dot comme un employé
fr.summary: Tout suivre dans l’unique chat Dots ne marchait pas, alors l’auteur traite son Dot, Elminster, comme un ingénieur qu’il manage : Elminster documente dans un espace Notion l’état des projets, les prochaines étapes, les blocages et les décisions attendues, et ils font un 1:1 quotidien. Loin d’être parfait, dit-il, mais bien mieux que le seul chat.

es.title: Gestiona tu Dot como a un empleado
es.summary: Llevarlo todo en el único chat de Dots no funcionaba, así que el autor trata a su Dot, Elminster, como a un ingeniero a su cargo: Elminster documenta en un espacio de Notion el estado de los proyectos, próximos pasos, bloqueos y decisiones pendientes, y tienen un 1:1 diario. Dice que está lejos de ser perfecto, pero va mucho mejor que solo chatear.

de.title: Den eigenen Dot wie einen Mitarbeiter führen
de.summary: Alles im einen Dots-Chat zu verfolgen klappte nicht, also behandelt der Autor seinen Dot Elminster wie einen Engineer, den er führt: Elminster dokumentiert in einem Notion-Workspace Projektstand, nächste Schritte, Blocker und nötige Entscheidungen, und sie halten tägliche 1:1s. Weit von perfekt, sagt er, aber viel besser als reiner Chat.

items.author: 0xTeddet
items.text:
tonight at 19:00 i switch on 5 grok bot routines, and if they work i wake up to pull requests instead of a to-do list

here's every one, word for word, so you can steal them:

01:00 → builder
"take the top 3 cards in todo. build each one on its own branch, run the tests, open a pull request with a 3-line summary. skip anything in not in v1"

03:00 → checker
"review every open pull request against done when. test it the way a student would. mark it ready for review or file a bug card with exact steps"

04:30 → builder, round 2
"take tonight's bug cards. fix anything under 30 minutes and leave the rest with a note"

05:30 → ops
"check uptime, error logs and the bot bill. one line each, no fixes"

06:30 → report to me
"send me one message: what got built, what passed, what's blocked, what needs me. end with live payments: on or off"

the rule under all 5: nothing that needs my yes runs after midnight. merges, deploys and live keys wait until i'm awake

i'll post what they actually did tomorrow at 07:00, good or bad

the full weekend playbook is in the article below

zh-CN.title: 5 个夜间 Grok Bot 例程：醒来看到 PR 而不是待办
zh-CN.summary: 作者设了 5 个按时间运行的 Grok Bot 例程：1 点构建待办前 3 张卡并开 PR，3 点审查 PR 或提 bug 卡，4:30 修 30 分钟内的 bug，5:30 查在线状态、错误日志和费用，6:30 发一条汇报。规则是午夜后不做任何需要他确认的事，合并、部署和正式密钥等他醒来再处理。

zh-TW.title: 5 個夜間 Grok Bot 例程：醒來看到 PR 而不是待辦
zh-TW.summary: 作者設了 5 個按時間執行的 Grok Bot 例程：1 點建置待辦前 3 張卡並開 PR，3 點審查 PR 或提 bug 卡，4:30 修 30 分鐘內的 bug，5:30 查線上狀態、錯誤日誌和費用，6:30 發一則匯報。規則是午夜後不做任何需要他確認的事，合併、部署和正式金鑰等他醒來再處理。

en.title: Five overnight Grok Bot routines: wake up to pull requests, not a to-do list
en.summary: The author scheduled five Grok Bot routines: at 1:00 build the top 3 todo cards and open PRs, at 3:00 review PRs or file bug cards, at 4:30 fix bugs under 30 minutes, at 5:30 check uptime, error logs and the bill, at 6:30 send one report. The rule: nothing that needs his yes runs after midnight; merges, deploys and live keys wait until he is awake.

ja.title: 夜間に動く5つのGrok Botルーティン：朝起きたらToDoではなくPR

ko.title: 밤새 도는 Grok Bot 루틴 5개: 아침엔 할 일 목록 대신 PR
ko.summary: 작성자는 Grok Bot 루틴 5개를 예약했다. 1시에 할 일 상위 3개 카드를 구현해 PR을 열고, 3시에 PR을 검토하거나 버그 카드를 만들고, 4시 30분에 30분 안에 고칠 수 있는 버그를 수정하고, 5시 30분에 가동 상태·오류 로그·비용을 확인하고, 6시 30분에 보고 한 통을 보낸다. 자정 이후에는 그의 승인이 필요한 일은 하지 않으며, 병합·배포·실서비스 키는 그가 깬 뒤로 미룬다.

ms.title: Lima rutin Grok Bot waktu malam: bangun dengan pull request, bukan senarai tugasan

Peraturannya: tiada apa yang memerlukan persetujuannya berjalan selepas tengah malam; merge, deploy dan kunci live menunggu dia bangun.

Quy tắc: sau nửa đêm không chạy việc gì cần anh đồng ý; merge, deploy và khóa live chờ anh thức dậy.

Règle : rien qui nécessite son accord ne tourne après minuit ; merges, déploiements et clés de production attendent son réveil.

Regla: nada que requiera su aprobación corre después de medianoche; merges, despliegues y claves en vivo esperan a que despierte.

I've been using GrokBot to automate video creation, but I kept running into the same problem.

Some videos looked amazing. Others had frustrating editing mistakes, awkward timing, or simply didn't meet my standards.

So I made two important changes.

1️⃣ I connected GrokBot to API Hub

👉 https://t.co/l3cM68Is27

A powerful platform we built that lets AI agents create and edit high-quality videos and automate the entire content production workflow.

This was a massive upgrade.

But even with better tools, occasional editing mistakes still slipped through.

And this changed everything.

Now, before any video gets published, GrokBot runs a quality assurance check.

It reviews the video, catches potential issues, and helps make sure the final result meets my standards.

No video gets published without passing QA.

The biggest lesson?

AI automation isn't just about generating content faster.

It's about building a system that checks its own work.

items.author: ellowmeAI
items.text:
YOUR FIRST GROK BOT SHOULD BE BORING ENOUGH TO TRUST.

most people see “AI teammate” and immediately design an org chart: a stack of roles, every available tool, and a vague mission to “run the business.”

it looks ambitious. it is also impossible to debug when the output goes wrong.

the smarter first move is narrower. give one Grok Bot one workflow with a visible finish line. every morning, it reviews unread customer emails, groups them by urgency, researches the missing context, and prepares replies for approval.

then judge the handoff, not the performance.

did it use the right sources? 
did it preserve context?
did it return at the right decision point? 
did it remove more work than it created?

if it fails, the scope is small enough to correct once and test again. if it works, you now have a repeatable unit that can expand without pretending to be an entire company.

the first useful Grok Bot will not feel like a new department.

it will feel like one task you stopped carrying.

zh-CN.title: 第一个 Grok Bot 要无聊到值得信任
zh-CN.summary: 作者建议别一上来就搭一整套角色组织，而是给一个 Grok Bot 一条有明确终点的流程：每天早上看未读客户邮件、按紧急度分组、补齐缺失背景、准备回复等你批准。然后评估交接：来源对不对、上下文是否保留、是否在该决策时交回、省的活是否多于添的活。

zh-TW.title: 第一個 Grok Bot 要無聊到值得信任
zh-TW.summary: 作者建議別一開始就搭一整套角色組織，而是給一個 Grok Bot 一條有明確終點的流程：每天早上看未讀客戶郵件、按緊急程度分組、補齊缺少的背景、準備回覆等你核准。然後評估交接：來源對不對、脈絡是否保留、是否在該決策時交回、省下的工作是否多於增加的。

en.title: Your first Grok Bot should be boring enough to trust
en.summary: Instead of designing an org chart of roles, the author suggests giving one Grok Bot one workflow with a visible finish line: every morning it reviews unread customer emails, groups them by urgency, researches missing context and prepares replies for approval. Then judge the handoff: right sources, preserved context, returning at the decision point, and removing more work than it creates.

ja.title: 最初のGrok Botは信頼できるほど地味でいい
ja.summary: 役割を並べた組織図を作るより、1つのGrok Botにゴールが見える1つの業務を任せようと作者は提案する。毎朝、未読の顧客メールを確認し、緊急度で分類し、足りない背景を調べ、承認用の返信案を用意する。そのうえで、正しい情報源を使ったか、文脈を保ったか、判断の場面で戻してきたか、増やした仕事より減らした仕事が多いかで評価する。

ko.title: 첫 Grok Bot은 믿을 수 있을 만큼 지루해야 한다
ko.summary: 작성자는 역할을 잔뜩 나눈 조직도 대신 Grok Bot 하나에 끝이 분명한 업무 하나를 맡기라고 권한다. 매일 아침 읽지 않은 고객 이메일을 검토하고, 긴급도별로 묶고, 빠진 맥락을 조사하고, 승인용 답장을 준비한다. 그다음 인계를 평가한다: 올바른 출처, 맥락 유지, 결정 시점에 돌아왔는지, 만든 일보다 줄인 일이 많은지.

ms.title: Grok Bot pertama anda patut cukup membosankan untuk dipercayai
ms.summary: Daripada mereka carta organisasi penuh peranan, penulis mencadangkan satu Grok Bot untuk satu aliran kerja dengan garis penamat yang jelas: setiap pagi ia menyemak e-mel pelanggan yang belum dibaca, mengumpulkannya ikut keutamaan, mencari konteks yang hilang dan menyediakan balasan untuk diluluskan. Kemudian nilai serahannya: sumber betul, konteks terpelihara, kembali pada titik keputusan, dan mengurangkan lebih banyak kerja daripada yang ditambah.

vi.title: Grok Bot đầu tiên nên đủ nhàm chán để tin được
vi.summary: Thay vì vẽ cả sơ đồ tổ chức nhiều vai trò, tác giả gợi ý giao cho một Grok Bot một quy trình có đích rõ ràng: mỗi sáng xem email khách hàng chưa đọc, nhóm theo mức khẩn, tìm bối cảnh còn thiếu và soạn sẵn trả lời chờ duyệt. Sau đó đánh giá khâu bàn giao: đúng nguồn, giữ ngữ cảnh, trả lại đúng lúc cần quyết định, và bớt việc nhiều hơn là tạo thêm.

fr.title: Votre premier Grok Bot doit être assez ennuyeux pour qu'on lui fasse confiance
fr.summary: Plutôt qu'un organigramme de rôles, l'auteur conseille de confier à un seul Grok Bot un seul flux avec une ligne d'arrivée claire : chaque matin, relire les e-mails clients non lus, les classer par urgence, chercher le contexte manquant et préparer des réponses à approuver. Puis juger la passation : bonnes sources, contexte préservé, retour au bon moment de décision, et plus de travail retiré qu'ajouté.

es.title: Tu primer Grok Bot debe ser lo bastante aburrido como para confiar en él
es.summary: En lugar de diseñar un organigrama de roles, el autor propone dar a un solo Grok Bot un solo flujo con meta visible: cada mañana revisa los correos de clientes sin leer, los agrupa por urgencia, investiga el contexto que falta y prepara respuestas para aprobar. Luego se evalúa la entrega: fuentes correctas, contexto preservado, vuelta en el punto de decisión y si quita más trabajo del que crea.

de.title: Dein erster Grok Bot sollte langweilig genug sein, um ihm zu vertrauen
de.summary: Statt eines Organigramms voller Rollen rät der Autor, einem Grok Bot einen Ablauf mit klarem Ziel zu geben: jeden Morgen ungelesene Kundenmails prüfen, nach Dringlichkeit gruppieren, fehlenden Kontext recherchieren und Antworten zur Freigabe vorbereiten. Dann die Übergabe bewerten: richtige Quellen, erhaltener Kontext, Rückmeldung am Entscheidungspunkt und mehr Arbeit abgenommen als erzeugt.

i made a video guide on how to use Grok Bot for FREE (version) on Windows 👇

➜ Step 1: Open your browser and go to this link:
https://t.co/nu91vGhPtD

➜ Step 2: Click “Download for Windows” and open the setup file from your downloads.

➜ Step 3: Run the installer. Choose who to install it for, click Next, pick a folder, then click Install.

➜ Step 4: Open Grok Bot and connect your X account.

➜ Step 5: Click your profile, go to Settings, then Usage & Billing.

➜ Step 6: Click Manage Plan. You’ll see you’re on the Free plan. Add your card (Mastercard or Visa) to set up billing.

➜ Step 7: Go to https://t.co/rakCeyUtrn, click Sign in, choose X, and click “Authorize app”.

✅ That’s it. Grok Bot is ready to use.

Follow @lionieio for more guides like this.

items.author: xbtvivi
items.text:
YOU ARE PAYING SENIOR RATES TO RENAME FILES

the setup everyone is reposting is OpenAI Dots plus Claude Code as one dev team. the part actually worth stealing is smaller than that: which model gets the task first.

Sonnet 5.5 reads at $2 per million and writes at $10. Opus 5.5 is double on both.

~/project-x $ claude -p "Fix issue #381. Run the tests. Open a pull request." --model claude-sonnet-5-5

here's the split:

▸ Sonnet takes the first pass on everything, 2 tries maximum
▸ Opus gets it only when Sonnet is stuck, 1 try, and it plans instead of typing
▸ tests decide, not the model. 318 of 318 or the task is not done
▸ you approve the pull request, and nothing merges itself

on 1,000 tasks that is roughly $480 instead of $800 for the same work, because the expensive brain only wakes up for the 20% that earns it.

the part that makes this safe: the Dot never merges. it opens the issue, reads the result and writes you a summary. the branch, the commits and the test output all live in GitHub, so neither model has to remember anything.

by 08:00 there is a PR waiting with no database changes and your approval missing, not a commit you have to undo.

the benchmarks are closer than that price gap suggests. Sonnet beats Opus on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 70.6 to 66.4. Opus pulls ahead on the long messy ones, FrontierCode 54.4 to 46.2. that spread is the entire reason a router exists.

one honest warning: there is no connect button. OpenAI and Anthropic ship nothing that joins these two. you build the GitHub bridge yourself, and if your tests are weak you have only automated a bad merge faster.

8 hours of nothing becomes 9 tasks routed, fixed and green before you open the laptop.

save it, this is the cheapest senior engineer you will ever avoid hiring.

items.author: Bagel8343
items.text:
How to choose between Muse and Grok Bot

The least useful agent comparison copies two feature lists and declares a winner. In practice, a disconnected tool, an unusable deliverable, or an unexpected action can matter more than the length of either list.

My recommendation is a testing order: start with Meta Muse for personal administration and goals; evaluate Grok Bot first for named responsibilities, recurring deliverables, and work across tools. Their capabilities overlap. This is a reading of official materials checked on October 28, 2026, not a head-to-head performance result.

Start with how the work is organized

Meta introduced Muse on September 8 and announced its Japan launch on October 23. These are existing developments, not news breaking today. Its positioning centers on a person’s goals, schedule, and everyday administration. [1] [2]

Grok Bot emphasizes named Bots with defined jobs and durable working context. Its skills describe how work is done; routines determine when it runs. [3] [4] That makes it worth testing first when you want an ongoing industry researcher and a separate editorial responsibility.

This is a preference, not a capability wall. Muse’s design article also describes a terminal, document and webpage creation, and continuing background work. [5] It is not limited to personal errands. Compare how much explanation and correction each product needs for your recurring tasks.

Check eligibility before designing the workflow. A regional Muse announcement does not establish worldwide access. Grok Bot’s current documentation lists compatible Cursor and SuperGrok subscriptions, among others; an X badge alone is not sufficient evidence of access. [2] [3] Verify the actual plan, limits, and connections available to your account.

The overlooked distinction is the permission boundary

Grok Bot’s detailed documentation says that Bots on the same account share a cloud computer, including files, browser sessions, and command-line credentials. Separate screens are not separate security boundaries. [6] Naming three Bots Researcher, Finance Assistant, and Personal Assistant does not automatically isolate their data.

Sharing makes handoffs easier: another Bot can continue saved work. It also changes what belongs in that environment. If clients or data classifications require strict separation, role descriptions are insufficient. Verify the product’s account or organizational isolation options; do not connect the data if those controls fail your requirements.

Muse’s security article describes separating the agent runtime from sensitive services, with an independent Sentinel controlling connector actions and network egress. [7] That is a vendor-disclosed architecture, not my security audit or proof of zero risk. Neither product’s documentation establishes that the other is necessarily unsafe.

Test a complete workflow

Consider a weekly technology brief. My proposed workflow is to collect specified sources with event dates, shortlist three candidates, prepare bilingual copy and illustrations, verify facts and calculations, and check that delivered files open. Stop at a reviewable draft. Missing sources should produce a gap report, not recycled figures presented as current.

In Grok Bot, start with one Bot completing the whole task before splitting research and editing. Its documentation recommends validating a one-time task before saving a skill and scheduling a routine. [4] Adding Bots too early may add handoff and debugging costs. Apply identical acceptance criteria to Muse; a terminal and file-generation capability do not establish delivery quality.

Define authorization separately for sending, purchasing, and publishing. Grok Bot documents approvals and Auto Review rules: Ask first takes precedence when it also matches an Allow automatically rule. Muse describes confirmation for consequential actions too. [1] [8] The account, recipient, and exact version must be identifiable. Website operation does not establish permission for every platform automation. Validate drafting and publishing separately.

The revealing cases are an expired login, an inaccessible source, or a damaged attachment. Does it stop and explain, or claim completion? Can it resume from a checkpoint without repeating an external action? Include those cases rather than judging only a smooth demonstration.

Price your review time as well as the subscription

Take a hypothetical example unrelated to either product’s actual plans. Suppose one option costs an extra $20 per month but saves two human minutes per accepted task. At $30 per hour, that releases $1 of time value per task. Twenty tasks cover the extra fee; 10 release $10 and 50 release $50.

The break-even assumes no additional setup or recovery cost. Extra costs raise the required volume. Released time is not necessarily cash savings: it matters only if time is actually freed and the opportunity-cost assumption is meaningful. Free entry does not mean zero total cost, and a higher fee does not establish better capability.

I would test the same 10 tasks on both products, repeating each batch twice: five sourced research summaries, three content deliverables, and two spreadsheet outputs. Keep sources, acceptance criteria, and budgets equal. Add expired-login and missing-source tests. If a product cannot deliver an item, record that instead of quietly substituting an easier task.

Track acceptable deliverables, human review minutes per task, serious errors, recovery outcomes, and total costs. Include failed attempts and rework. Ten tasks are a starting point, not proof of general reliability. The goal is to choose for your work, not crown a universal winner.

My decision

For personal preferences and life administration, I would start with Muse. For recurring research, file delivery, and explicit responsibilities, I would evaluate Grok Bot first. That preference follows their product organization, not a ranking of model intelligence.

If the necessary connection, regional access, subscription, or data separation is missing, postpone the migration. Watch recovery, visible permissions, accepted-delivery rate, and review effort—not only new model names. Keep the product that reduces repeated explanation and rework on your tasks.

Primary sources

[1] Meta  Introducing Muse https://t.co/otn9A3xQtI

[2] Meta Japan  Muse launches in Japan https://t.co/xawKFU9XXJ

[3] Grok Bot Docs  Overview https://t.co/6omTXiaBuu

[4] Grok Bot Docs  Skills and routines https://t.co/tBTQE5Q2tv

[5] Muse  How We Designed Muse https://t.co/jM044YbDVg

[6] Grok Bot Docs  Use the computer and apps https://t.co/aZysmtA4yI

[7] Meta AI Research  How We Built Safety Into Muse https://t.co/ymGiqmS90z

[8] Grok Bot Docs  Approvals security and privacy https://t.co/k6f6Nw9yeA

ja.summary: 作者は2026年10月28日時点の公式資料をもとに試す順番を提案。個人の好みや生活の事務はまずMeta Muse、定期的なリサーチやファイル納品、明確な担当業務はまずGrok Botを評価する。実際のタスク約10件で、受け入れ可能な成果物、確認にかかった時間、重大なミス、復旧、総コストを記録する。実測の優劣ではないと明記している。

ko.summary: 작성자는 2026년 10월 28일 기준 공식 자료를 바탕으로 시험 순서를 제안한다. 개인 취향과 생활 관리에는 Meta Muse부터, 반복 리서치·파일 전달·명확한 책임이 있는 업무에는 Grok Bot부터 평가한다. 실제 작업 약 10개로 수용 가능한 결과물, 검토 시간, 심각한 오류, 복구, 총비용을 기록하라고 한다. 실측 순위가 아니라고 강조한다.

ms.title: Memilih antara Muse dan Grok Bot ikut cara kerja disusun, bukan senarai ciri
ms.summary: Berdasarkan bahan rasmi setakat 2026-10-28, penulis mencadangkan urutan percubaan: mula dengan Meta Muse untuk keutamaan peribadi dan urusan hidup, dan nilai Grok Bot dahulu untuk penyelidikan berulang, penghantaran fail dan tanggungjawab yang jelas. Jalankan kira-kira sepuluh tugas sebenar dan jejak hasil yang diterima, minit semakan, ralat serius, pemulihan dan jumlah kos. Dia menegaskan ini bukan ranking yang diuji.

vi.title: Chọn Muse hay Grok Bot theo cách tổ chức công việc, không theo danh sách tính năng
vi.summary: Dựa trên tài liệu chính thức tính đến 28/10/2026, tác giả gợi ý thứ tự thử: việc cá nhân và quản lý đời sống thì thử Meta Muse trước; nghiên cứu định kỳ, bàn giao tệp và trách nhiệm rõ ràng thì đánh giá Grok Bot trước. Chạy khoảng 10 việc thật và theo dõi sản phẩm đạt yêu cầu, số phút rà soát, lỗi nghiêm trọng, khả năng khôi phục và tổng chi phí. Anh nhấn mạnh đây không phải xếp hạng đã kiểm chứng.

fr.title: Choisir entre Muse et Grok Bot selon l'organisation du travail, pas les listes de fonctions
fr.summary: D'après les documents officiels au 28 octobre 2026, l'auteur propose un ordre d'essai : commencer par Meta Muse pour les préférences personnelles et l'administratif du quotidien, et évaluer d'abord Grok Bot pour la recherche récurrente, la livraison de fichiers et les responsabilités explicites. Tester une dizaine de tâches réelles en suivant livrables acceptables, minutes de relecture, erreurs graves, récupération et coût total. Ce n'est pas un classement testé, précise-t-il.

es.title: Elegir entre Muse y Grok Bot según cómo se organiza el trabajo, no por listas de funciones
es.summary: Con material oficial a fecha del 28 de octubre de 2026, el autor propone un orden de prueba: empezar con Meta Muse para preferencias personales y trámites cotidianos, y evaluar primero Grok Bot para investigación recurrente, entrega de archivos y responsabilidades explícitas. Probar unas diez tareas reales midiendo entregas aceptables, minutos de revisión, errores graves, recuperación y costo total. Aclara que no es un ranking probado.

de.title: Muse oder Grok Bot: nach Arbeitsorganisation wählen, nicht nach Feature-Listen
de.summary: Auf Basis offizieller Unterlagen mit Stand 28.10.2026 schlägt der Autor eine Testreihenfolge vor: für persönliche Vorlieben und Alltagsorganisation zuerst Meta Muse, für wiederkehrende Recherche, Dateilieferung und klare Zuständigkeiten zuerst Grok Bot prüfen. Etwa zehn echte Aufgaben testen und brauchbare Ergebnisse, Prüfminuten, schwere Fehler, Wiederherstellung und Gesamtkosten erfassen. Er betont, dass es kein getestetes Ranking ist.

items.text:
Meta Museの興味深い利用例（Xユーザー・実例中心） $META

お金・請求まわり
•電話・ネット回線の値引き交渉（実際に電話もかける）：AT&Tを$80→$40、Spectrumを$75→$40、Verizonを$516→$386など。Peter Yang氏は年$800超節約したと報告。
•自動車保険の見直し：$3,500/年節約（同じ補償）、別事例では$500→$335/月に当日切り替え。
•フライト遅延補償：7時間遅延でDeltaから$250クレジットを約5分で取得＋再予約。
•運賃下落監視：予約済みフライトを監視して値下がり時にクレジット取得（$1,000超の例あり）。
•未請求金の発見：州の未請求財産から$1,500超を5分程度で見つけ、申請書類まで作成。
•サブスク監査：メールや明細を見て使っていないものを解約し、月$100超・年$1,200相当の節約例。

旅行・予約
•日本旅行のレストラン予約を全部Museに任せ、箱根のホテルに日本語で交渉して非公開ディナーを確保した例。
•フライト・ホテル・移動・レストランを一気に組む。カレンダー連携で空き時間を見て予約。

生活・その他
•Facebook Marketplaceで出品・交渉・購入者対応。
•「タコスの火曜日」みたいな曖昧な指示からInstacartでカート作成〜決済まで。
•古いメール数万通の整理、返品手続き、HVACメンテ予約など、面倒な事務作業をまとめて処理。
•求人応募を数十件自動化して面接まで進めた例。
•イベント準備（ボランティア登録・メール対応・スケジュール作成）を任せて、当日は行くだけ。

傾向 特に「請求交渉・保険見直し・返金・未請求金」が突出して効果を出しており、Xでも「Museが一番使ってるAIになった」「Claude解約した」といった声が見られます。買い物・予約系も多いですが、Amazonはブロックするなどサイトによる制限もあります。
（多くは自己報告ベースなので、実際の結果はケースバイケースです）

fr.summary: L'auteur rassemble des cas Muse vus sur X : négocier par téléphone des forfaits téléphone et internet, par exemple AT&T de 80 $ à 40 $, Peter Yang déclarant plus de 800 $ économisés par an ; une révision d'assurance auto économisant 3 500 $ par an ; un avoir Delta de 250 $ obtenu en environ 5 minutes après 7 h de retard ; plus de 1 500 $ de biens non réclamés retrouvés ; plus audit d'abonnements, réservations au Japon, ventes sur Marketplace, commandes Instacart et candidatures en masse. items.author: yasutaketin
items.text:
MuseはAmazonにブロックされて買い物出来ないの？ $META $AMZN

はい、Amazonでは買い物できません。
AmazonはMeta Museのローンチ直後（2026年9月中旬頃）から、Museによるhttps://t.co/j1CQEwpazcへのアクセスをブロックしています。
状況
•MuseでAmazonを開こうとすると、「Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use」というポップアップが出て進めない。
•Amazon側は「事前に許可を求めていない」「エージェントが自分を名乗らない」「ログイン情報を扱うリスクがある」として、MetaにAmazonをMuseの対象から外すよう要請したが、応じなかったためブロックした、と説明しています。
背景 Amazonは自社の「Buy for Me」などのエージェントを推進しつつ、他社のエージェント（以前はPerplexityなども）が自サイトで買い物するのを積極的に防いでいます。Muse以外にも、一部の小売業者がエージェントによる購入を拒否する動きが出ています。
代わりにできること
•Walmart、Best Buy、Sephora、Wayfair、Shopify系店舗など、Museと連携している店舗や、ブロックされていないサイトでは買い物可能。
•Amazon以外の一般的なサイトなら、ブラウザ経由で操作できるケースが多いです。
現状、Amazonでの買い物は事実上使えない状態です。

zh-CN.title: 注意：Meta Muse 无法在 Amazon 购物

zh-TW.title: 注意：Meta Muse 無法在 Amazon 購物

en.title: Heads-up: Meta Muse can't shop on Amazon
en.summary: The author explains that since Muse launched in mid-September 2026, Amazon has blocked Muse from its site, showing a popup that continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates its Conditions of Use. Amazon says Meta didn't ask permission, the agent doesn't identify itself, and handling login details is risky. Alternatives are sites that aren't blocked, such as Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair and Shopify stores.

ja.title: 注意：Meta MuseはAmazonで買い物できない
ja.summary: 作者によると、2026年9月中旬のMuse公開直後からAmazonはMuseのアクセスをブロックしており、開くと許可のないAIエージェントの利用は利用規約違反だというポップアップが出る。Amazonは、事前に許可を求めていない、エージェントが名乗らない、ログイン情報を扱うリスクがあると説明。代わりにWalmart、Best Buy、Sephora、Wayfair、Shopify系店舗などブロックされていないサイトで買い物できる。

ko.title: 주의: Meta Muse는 Amazon에서 쇼핑할 수 없다
ko.summary: 작성자에 따르면 2026년 9월 중순 Muse 출시 직후부터 Amazon은 Muse의 접근을 차단했고, 열면 승인되지 않은 AI 에이전트의 접근은 이용 약관 위반이라는 팝업이 뜬다. Amazon은 사전 허가 요청이 없었고, 에이전트가 신원을 밝히지 않으며, 로그인 정보 처리 위험이 있다고 설명한다. 대안은 Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair, Shopify 매장처럼 차단되지 않은 사이트다.

ms.title: Perhatian: Meta Muse tidak boleh membeli-belah di Amazon
ms.summary: Penulis menjelaskan sejak Muse dilancarkan pertengahan September 2026, Amazon menyekat Muse daripada lamannya, dengan pop timbul bahawa akses berterusan oleh ejen AI tanpa kebenaran melanggar Syarat Penggunaannya. Amazon berkata Meta tidak meminta izin, ejen tidak mengenal pasti dirinya, dan mengendalikan butiran log masuk berisiko. Alternatifnya ialah laman yang tidak disekat seperti Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair dan kedai Shopify.

vi.title: Lưu ý: Meta Muse không mua sắm được trên Amazon
vi.summary: Tác giả giải thích từ khi Muse ra mắt giữa tháng 9/2026, Amazon đã chặn Muse truy cập trang, hiện thông báo rằng truy cập của tác tử AI không được phép là vi phạm điều khoản sử dụng. Amazon nói Meta không xin phép trước, tác tử không tự nhận danh tính và việc xử lý thông tin đăng nhập là rủi ro. Có thể mua ở các trang không bị chặn như Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair và các cửa hàng Shopify.

fr.title: Attention : Meta Muse ne peut pas acheter sur Amazon
fr.summary: L'auteur explique que depuis le lancement de Muse mi-septembre 2026, Amazon bloque Muse sur son site avec une fenêtre indiquant que l'accès par un agent IA non autorisé viole ses conditions d'utilisation. Amazon reproche à Meta de ne pas avoir demandé la permission, à l'agent de ne pas s'identifier, et le risque lié aux identifiants. Alternatives : les sites non bloqués comme Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair et les boutiques Shopify.

es.title: Aviso: Meta Muse no puede comprar en Amazon
es.summary: El autor explica que desde el lanzamiento de Muse a mediados de septiembre de 2026, Amazon bloquea a Muse en su sitio con un aviso de que el acceso de un agente de IA no autorizado viola sus Condiciones de Uso. Amazon dice que Meta no pidió permiso, que el agente no se identifica y que manejar credenciales es arriesgado. Como alternativa, sitios no bloqueados como Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair y tiendas Shopify.

de.title: Hinweis: Meta Muse kann nicht bei Amazon einkaufen
de.summary: Laut Autor blockiert Amazon Muse seit dem Start Mitte September 2026 und zeigt einen Hinweis, dass weiterer Zugriff durch einen nicht autorisierten KI-Agenten gegen die Nutzungsbedingungen verstößt. Amazon begründet das damit, dass Meta nicht um Erlaubnis bat, der Agent sich nicht zu erkennen gibt und der Umgang mit Zugangsdaten riskant ist. Alternativen sind nicht gesperrte Shops wie Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora, Wayfair und Shopify-Läden.

ms.summary: Dari EU, penulis menyatakan Claude Duet dan OpenAI dots tidak tersedia di sana, manakala Grok Bot tersedia dan melakukan kerja. Dia menggunakannya untuk menjejak aplikasi mana yang mendapat kemas kini Duo, memantau lambakan mesej supaya tiada yang terlepas, dan belajar bahasa Sepanyol.

vi.title: Đánh giá tác tử cá nhân từ EU: chỉ có Grok Bot dùng được
vi.summary: Ở EU, tác giả cho biết Claude Duet và OpenAI dots chưa có mặt, còn Grok Bot thì có và đang làm việc. Anh dùng nó để theo dõi ứng dụng nào có cập nhật Duo, canh dòng tin nhắn dồn dập để không sót gì, và học tiếng Tây Ban Nha.

fr.title: Avis sur les agents personnels depuis l'UE : seul Grok Bot est disponible
fr.summary: Depuis l'UE, l'auteur note que Claude Duet et OpenAI dots n'y sont pas disponibles, alors que Grok Bot l'est et fait le travail. Il s'en sert pour suivre quelles applis ont reçu des mises à jour Duo, surveiller le flot de messages pour ne rien rater, et apprendre l'espagnol.

es.title: Reseña de agentes personales desde la UE: solo Grok Bot está disponible
es.summary: Desde la UE, el autor señala que Claude Duet y OpenAI dots no están disponibles allí, mientras que Grok Bot sí y hace el trabajo. Lo usa para seguir qué apps recibieron actualizaciones de Duo, vigilar la avalancha de mensajes para que nada se escape y aprender español.

de.title: Persönliche Agenten aus EU-Sicht: Nur Grok Bot ist verfügbar
de.summary: Aus der EU schreibt der Autor, dass Claude Duet und OpenAI dots dort nicht verfügbar sind, Grok Bot dagegen schon und die Arbeit erledigt. Er nutzt ihn, um zu verfolgen, welche Apps Duo-Updates bekamen, die Nachrichtenflut im Blick zu behalten, damit nichts untergeht, und Spanisch zu lernen.

items.author: paraskarmachary
items.text:
In 10 weeks, 4 AI labs shipped personal agents that never log off.
Most researchers will hand them the wrong jobs.

This month I finished my April travel reimbursements.
6 months late.

Federally funded PIs spend an estimated 44% of research time on admin.
ChatGPT cleared my pile in one sitting. 
Then it hit me. An always-on agent would never let the pile form.

What I'd tell any researcher setting one up:

1️⃣ Decide what it handles without telling you
↳ Do: easy to undo. Filing receipts.
↳ Digest: weekly. New papers.
↳ Ping: urgent and rare. A retraction of a paper you cite.
↳ Ask: anything sent in your name.

2️⃣ Every extra alert makes you likelier to miss the urgent one
↳ Clinicians override 49% to 96% of drug safety alerts.
↳ Keep the Ping lane tiny.

3️⃣ Literature updates don't need an always-on agent
↳ A scheduled weekly search in Claude or ChatGPT is enough.
↳ Keep your PubMed alert as a scheduled task (personal AI agents is overkill).

4️⃣ What it can see matters more than how smart it is
↳ Mine reads my personal Gmail, not my institutional inbox. Work email and patient data wait for institutional approval.
↳ Meta just paused Muse's chat sharing after about 6,800 shared links surfaced in public DNS records.

5️⃣ Start with a job where a mistake is easy to undo
↳ Receipts, filed by meeting as they arrive. You still press submit.

One catch: Dots aren't on ChatGPT Plus, and Claude Duet is a US waitlist. 

💬 Which admin job would you hand off first?

More on AI for academic research in my free newsletter (16,000+ researchers): https://t.co/XTq6dj6SoB

zh-CN.title: 研究者设置常驻 AI 代理的 5 条建议
zh-CN.summary: 作者是科研人员：把代理的事分成直接做（易撤销，如归档收据）、每周摘要、少量紧急提醒、以你名义发出的事需先问；提醒越多越容易漏掉紧急的，所以提醒通道要小；文献更新用每周定时搜索就够；能看到什么比多聪明更重要，他只给个人 Gmail，不给机构邮箱；从容易撤销的事开始。

zh-TW.title: 研究者設定常駐 AI 代理的 5 條建議
zh-TW.summary: 作者是研究人員：把代理的事分成直接做（易撤銷，如歸檔收據）、每週摘要、少量緊急提醒、以你名義發出的事需先問；提醒越多越容易漏掉緊急的，所以提醒通道要小；文獻更新用每週排程搜尋就夠；能看到什麼比多聰明更重要，他只給個人 Gmail，不給機構信箱；從容易撤銷的事開始。

en.title: Five tips for researchers setting up an always-on agent
en.summary: A researcher's advice: sort jobs into Do (easy to undo, like filing receipts), weekly Digest, rare urgent Ping, and Ask for anything sent in your name; keep the Ping lane tiny since extra alerts hide urgent ones; a scheduled weekly search is enough for literature updates; what it can see matters more than how smart it is, so his reads personal Gmail, not his institutional inbox; and start with jobs that are easy to undo.

ja.title: 研究者が常時稼働エージェントを設定するための5つの助言
ja.summary: 研究者である作者の助言：仕事を「実行」（領収書の整理など取り消しやすいもの）、週次の「ダイジェスト」、緊急でまれな「通知」、自分の名前で送るものは「確認」に分ける。通知が増えると緊急の通知を見落とすので通知は最小限に。文献の更新は週1回の定期検索で十分。賢さより何が見えるかが重要で、作者は個人のGmailだけを読ませ、所属機関のメールは渡していない。取り消しやすい仕事から始める。

ko.title: 연구자가 상시 에이전트를 설정할 때의 팁 5가지
ko.summary: 연구자인 작성자의 조언: 일을 실행(영수증 정리처럼 되돌리기 쉬운 것), 주간 요약, 드물고 긴급한 알림, 내 이름으로 보내는 건 확인 요청으로 나눈다. 알림이 늘면 긴급한 것을 놓치므로 알림 채널은 작게. 논문 업데이트는 주간 예약 검색이면 충분하다. 똑똑함보다 무엇을 볼 수 있는지가 중요해 그는 개인 Gmail만 읽게 하고 기관 메일은 주지 않는다. 되돌리기 쉬운 일부터 시작하라.

ms.title: Lima petua untuk penyelidik yang menyediakan ejen sentiasa aktif
ms.summary: Nasihat seorang penyelidik: bahagikan kerja kepada Buat (mudah dibatalkan, seperti memfailkan resit), Ringkasan mingguan, Ping segera yang jarang, dan Tanya untuk apa-apa yang dihantar atas nama anda; kecilkan saluran Ping kerana amaran berlebihan menyembunyikan yang penting; carian mingguan berjadual cukup untuk kemas kini kajian; apa yang ia boleh lihat lebih penting daripada kepintarannya, jadi miliknya membaca Gmail peribadi, bukan peti institusi; dan mula dengan kerja yang mudah dibatalkan.

vi.title: 5 lời khuyên cho nhà nghiên cứu khi thiết lập tác tử luôn bật
vi.summary: Lời khuyên của một nhà nghiên cứu: chia việc thành Làm (dễ hoàn tác, như lưu hóa đơn), Tóm tắt hằng tuần, Báo gấp hiếm khi, và Hỏi trước với mọi thứ gửi dưới tên bạn; giữ kênh báo gấp thật nhỏ vì quá nhiều cảnh báo làm lấp việc gấp; cập nhật tài liệu chỉ cần tìm kiếm định kỳ hằng tuần; thứ nó nhìn thấy quan trọng hơn độ thông minh, nên anh chỉ cho đọc Gmail cá nhân, không cho hộp thư cơ quan; và bắt đầu với việc dễ hoàn tác.

fr.title: Cinq conseils aux chercheurs qui configurent un agent toujours actif
fr.summary: Conseils d'un chercheur : classer les tâches en Faire (facile à annuler, comme ranger des reçus), Résumé hebdomadaire, Alerte urgente et rare, et Demander pour tout ce qui part en votre nom ; garder les alertes au minimum, car trop d'alertes masquent l'urgent ; une recherche hebdomadaire planifiée suffit pour la veille bibliographique ; ce que l'agent voit compte plus que son intelligence, donc le sien lit son Gmail perso, pas sa boîte institutionnelle ; et commencer par des tâches faciles à annuler.

es.title: Cinco consejos para investigadores que configuran un agente siempre activo
es.summary: Consejos de un investigador: dividir las tareas en Hacer (fácil de deshacer, como archivar recibos), Resumen semanal, Aviso urgente y poco frecuente, y Preguntar para todo lo que se envía en tu nombre; mantener mínimo el canal de avisos porque el exceso oculta lo urgente; una búsqueda semanal programada basta para la literatura; importa más lo que puede ver que lo listo que es, así que el suyo lee su Gmail personal, no el correo institucional; y empezar por tareas fáciles de deshacer.

de.title: Fünf Tipps für Forschende, die einen dauerhaft aktiven Agenten einrichten
de.summary: Rat eines Forschers: Aufgaben in Erledigen (leicht rückgängig zu machen, etwa Belege ablegen), wöchentlichen Digest, seltenen dringenden Ping und Nachfragen bei allem, was in deinem Namen rausgeht, aufteilen; den Ping-Kanal klein halten, weil zu viele Alarme das Dringende verdecken; für Literatur genügt eine geplante Wochensuche; wichtiger als Intelligenz ist, was er sehen darf, daher liest seiner das private Gmail, nicht das Dienstpostfach; und mit leicht umkehrbaren Aufgaben beginnen.

items.author: pocarles
items.text:
I won't pick a daily driver for my autonomous agent before I've tried @Claude Duet.

So far, I like @OpenAI Dot. It looks very promising, but it doesn't evolve much, at least from what I see, and it can't safely drive more than 2 or 3 sessions in parallel.

@Muse is surprisingly good and polished, maybe the most proactive of them all. But it doesn't feel built for work, and I don't need an agent to find me a hotel. I don't even let my wife do that.

Then there's Grok @bot. I have one for X, but I haven't gone deep with it. It was really dumb a few times at the beginning, and I lost the little trust I'd given it. The hype is real, though, and half of tech bro Twitter is rooting for it, including people I respect like @theo. It has to be good. I want to believe.

I still have a Hermes agent. I love it for research and for discussing ideas, not for doing the actual work. And I have an OpenClaw agent enjoying an early retirement. You can call it nostalgia. 6 months feels like a century in AI land.

Now, I have big hopes for Duet because, on paper, it's built for people like me: small business owners juggling way too many balls. Like OpenAI Dot, it would have access to my repos, hundreds of sessions, skills, plugins and historical data. An agent needs context, and seriously good access to Codex and Claude.

To make up my mind while waiting for Duet, I'm closely following a few people who build these projects or have real influence on them. An agent, alone or running a swarm, takes time to set up properly in your ecosystem before it gives its best, and I don't have the bandwidth to do that 2 or 3 times.

We are back to the Android vs iOS thing, where you definitely need to pick a side if you want the best of it.

If you are in a similar situation and don't follow them yet, start here: @ahuja_karan, @gabemulley, @embirico, @TheRohanVarma, @christinesed, @dps, @poteto (of course!) and @romanugarte.

zh-CN.title: 一位小企业主对比 Dot、Muse、Grok Bot 和 Hermes
zh-CN.summary: 作者说 OpenAI Dot 很有前景但进化不多，且无法安全并行超过 2 到 3 个会话；Muse 精致且最主动，但不像为工作而做；他用于 X 的 Grok Bot 起初几次表现很笨，让他失去了信任；Hermes 适合研究和讨论想法，不适合实际干活。他在等 Claude Duet 再决定主力，因为把代理接入自己的生态很花时间。

zh-TW.title: 一位小企業主比較 Dot、Muse、Grok Bot 和 Hermes
zh-TW.summary: 作者說 OpenAI Dot 很有前景但進化不多，且無法安全並行超過 2 到 3 個工作階段；Muse 精緻且最主動，但不像為工作而做；他用於 X 的 Grok Bot 起初幾次表現很笨，讓他失去了信任；Hermes 適合研究和討論想法，不適合實際做事。他在等 Claude Duet 再決定主力，因為把代理接入自己的生態很花時間。

en.title: A small business owner compares Dot, Muse, Grok Bot and Hermes
en.summary: The author finds OpenAI Dot promising but slow to evolve, and it can't safely drive more than 2 or 3 sessions in parallel; Muse is polished and the most proactive but doesn't feel built for work; his Grok Bot for X was dumb a few times early on and lost his trust; Hermes is good for research and discussing ideas, not doing the work. He is waiting for Claude Duet before picking a daily driver, since setting up an agent takes time.

ja.title: 小規模事業者がDot・Muse・Grok Bot・Hermesを比較
ja.summary: 作者の評価：OpenAI Dotは有望だが進化が少なく、並行で安全に動かせるのは2〜3セッションまで。Museは洗練されていて最も能動的だが仕事向きではない。X用に使っているGrok Botは最初に何度かお粗末な動きをして信頼を失った。Hermesはリサーチや議論には良いが実作業向きではない。エージェントの導入には時間がかかるため、Claude Duetを試してから常用を決めるという。

ko.title: 소상공인이 비교한 Dot, Muse, Grok Bot, Hermes
ko.summary: 작성자 평가: OpenAI Dot은 유망하지만 발전이 더디고 2~3개 넘는 세션을 안전하게 병렬로 돌리지 못한다. Muse는 세련되고 가장 능동적이지만 업무용 같지 않다. X용 Grok Bot은 초반에 몇 번 엉뚱하게 굴어 신뢰를 잃었다. Hermes는 리서치와 아이디어 논의에는 좋지만 실제 작업용은 아니다. 에이전트 설정에 시간이 들기 때문에 Claude Duet을 써본 뒤 주력을 정하겠다고 한다.

ms.title: Pemilik perniagaan kecil membandingkan Dot, Muse, Grok Bot dan Hermes
ms.summary: Penulis mendapati OpenAI Dot menjanjikan tetapi lambat berkembang, dan tidak boleh menjalankan lebih 2 atau 3 sesi selari dengan selamat; Muse kemas dan paling proaktif tetapi tidak terasa dibina untuk kerja; Grok Bot miliknya untuk X beberapa kali bodoh pada awalnya dan hilang kepercayaannya; Hermes bagus untuk penyelidikan dan berbincang idea, bukan membuat kerja. Dia menunggu Claude Duet sebelum memilih, kerana menyediakan ejen mengambil masa.

vi.title: Một chủ doanh nghiệp nhỏ so sánh Dot, Muse, Grok Bot và Hermes
vi.summary: Tác giả thấy OpenAI Dot hứa hẹn nhưng ít tiến triển, và không chạy song song an toàn quá 2–3 phiên; Muse chỉn chu và chủ động nhất nhưng không giống công cụ làm việc; Grok Bot anh dùng cho X vài lần đầu xử lý ngớ ngẩn nên mất lòng tin; Hermes tốt cho nghiên cứu và bàn ý tưởng chứ không làm việc thật. Anh chờ thử Claude Duet rồi mới chọn, vì thiết lập một tác tử tốn thời gian.

fr.title: Un patron de petite entreprise compare Dot, Muse, Grok Bot et Hermes
fr.summary: Pour l'auteur, OpenAI Dot est prometteur mais évolue peu et ne peut pas gérer sans risque plus de 2 ou 3 sessions en parallèle ; Muse est soigné et le plus proactif, mais ne semble pas fait pour le travail ; son Grok Bot pour X a été bête plusieurs fois au début et a perdu sa confiance ; Hermes est bien pour la recherche et les idées, pas pour exécuter. Il attend Claude Duet avant de choisir, car configurer un agent prend du temps.

es.title: Un dueño de pequeña empresa compara Dot, Muse, Grok Bot y Hermes
es.summary: El autor ve OpenAI Dot prometedor pero con poca evolución, y no puede manejar con seguridad más de 2 o 3 sesiones en paralelo; Muse es pulido y el más proactivo, pero no parece hecho para trabajar; su Grok Bot para X fue torpe varias veces al principio y perdió su confianza; Hermes sirve para investigar y debatir ideas, no para hacer el trabajo. Espera a Claude Duet antes de elegir, porque configurar un agente lleva tiempo.

de.title: Ein Kleinunternehmer vergleicht Dot, Muse, Grok Bot und Hermes
de.summary: Der Autor hält OpenAI Dot für vielversprechend, aber es entwickelt sich kaum und kann nicht sicher mehr als 2 oder 3 Sitzungen parallel steuern; Muse ist ausgereift und am proaktivsten, wirkt aber nicht für die Arbeit gebaut; sein Grok Bot für X war anfangs einige Male dumm und verlor sein Vertrauen; Hermes taugt für Recherche und Ideen, nicht für die Ausführung. Er wartet auf Claude Duet, weil die Einrichtung eines Agenten Zeit kostet.

items.author: yasutaketin
items.text:
【Meta Museの価格と収益化予想まとめ】 $META

価格
•無料：週次制限あり。機能は有料とほぼ同じ
•Power：月$20、週5億トークン
•Maximum：月$100、週30億トークン
•有料は使用量拡張がメイン（機能差はほぼなし）
•現在はUS・カナダ限定テスト中

ChatGPT dotsとの違い
•dotsはPro（$100以上）必須
•Museは無料で試せるのが最大の差

Metaの収益化戦略
•本命はトランザクション手数料（買い物・予約など、事業者負担）
•買い物が最多利用で、平均購入額は$200超
•コンシューマー向けサブスク（Power/Maximum）
•ビジネス向け有料サービス
•Muse内に広告は入れない方針（Meta全体の広告改善に活用）
•「ほとんどの人は無料、ビジネスが負担」＋計算効率を1年で10倍改善で利益化を狙う

要するに、ユーザー獲得優先で収益は後乗せするMetaらしい攻めの設定。

zh-CN.title: Meta Muse 价格档位与额度，对比 ChatGPT dots
zh-CN.summary: 作者整理：Muse 免费版有每周限制、功能与付费版几乎相同；Power 每月 20 美元、每周 5 亿 token；Maximum 每月 100 美元、每周 30 亿 token；付费主要是扩额度，目前在美国和加拿大测试。相比之下 ChatGPT dots 需要 100 美元以上的 Pro 方案。作者还整理了 Meta 以交易手续费和订阅为主的变现思路。

zh-TW.title: Meta Muse 價格方案與額度，對比 ChatGPT dots
zh-TW.summary: 作者整理：Muse 免費版有每週限制、功能與付費版幾乎相同；Power 每月 20 美元、每週 5 億 token；Maximum 每月 100 美元、每週 30 億 token；付費主要是擴充額度，目前在美國和加拿大測試。相較之下 ChatGPT dots 需要 100 美元以上的 Pro 方案。作者也整理了 Meta 以交易手續費和訂閱為主的變現思路。

en.title: Meta Muse pricing tiers and token limits, compared with ChatGPT dots
en.summary: The author's summary: Muse Free has weekly limits but nearly the same features; Power is $20 a month with 500 million tokens a week; Maximum is $100 a month with 3 billion tokens a week; paid tiers mainly add usage, and testing is in the US and Canada. ChatGPT dots by contrast requires Pro at $100 or more. He also outlines Meta's expected monetization through transaction fees and subscriptions.

ja.title: Meta Museの料金プランと上限、ChatGPT dotsとの比較
ja.summary: 作者のまとめ：Museの無料版は週ごとの制限があるが機能は有料とほぼ同じ。Powerは月20ドルで週5億トークン、Maximumは月100ドルで週30億トークン。有料は主に使用量の拡張で、現在は米国とカナダでテスト中。一方ChatGPT dotsは100ドル以上のProが必須。取引手数料とサブスクを中心とするMetaの収益化予想も整理している。

ko.title: Meta Muse 요금제와 토큰 한도, ChatGPT dots와 비교
ko.summary: 작성자 요약: Muse 무료는 주간 한도가 있지만 기능은 유료와 거의 같다. Power는 월 20달러에 주 5억 토큰, Maximum은 월 100달러에 주 30억 토큰. 유료는 주로 사용량 확장이며 현재 미국과 캐나다에서 시험 중이다. 반면 ChatGPT dots는 100달러 이상인 Pro가 필수다. 거래 수수료와 구독 중심의 Meta 수익화 전망도 정리했다.

ms.title: Peringkat harga dan had token Meta Muse, berbanding ChatGPT dots
ms.summary: Ringkasan penulis: Muse Free ada had mingguan tetapi ciri hampir sama; Power $20 sebulan dengan 500 juta token seminggu; Maximum $100 sebulan dengan 3 bilion token seminggu; peringkat berbayar terutamanya menambah penggunaan, dan ujian di AS dan Kanada. ChatGPT dots pula memerlukan Pro pada $100 atau lebih. Dia juga menggariskan jangkaan pengewangan Meta melalui yuran transaksi dan langganan.

vi.title: Các gói giá và hạn mức token của Meta Muse, so với ChatGPT dots
vi.summary: Tóm tắt của tác giả: Muse Free có giới hạn hằng tuần nhưng tính năng gần như bản trả phí; Power 20 USD/tháng với 500 triệu token/tuần; Maximum 100 USD/tháng với 3 tỷ token/tuần; gói trả phí chủ yếu tăng hạn mức, hiện thử nghiệm ở Mỹ và Canada. Trong khi đó ChatGPT dots bắt buộc gói Pro từ 100 USD. Anh cũng phác thảo cách Meta dự kiến kiếm tiền qua phí giao dịch và thuê bao.

fr.title: Forfaits et limites de tokens de Meta Muse, comparés à ChatGPT dots
fr.summary: Résumé de l'auteur : Muse Free a des limites hebdomadaires mais presque les mêmes fonctions ; Power coûte 20 $ par mois pour 500 millions de tokens par semaine ; Maximum 100 $ par mois pour 3 milliards par semaine ; les offres payantes ajoutent surtout du volume, en test aux États-Unis et au Canada. ChatGPT dots exige au contraire Pro à 100 $ ou plus. Il esquisse aussi la monétisation attendue de Meta via commissions et abonnements.

es.title: Planes y límites de tokens de Meta Muse, comparados con ChatGPT dots
es.summary: Resumen del autor: Muse Free tiene límites semanales pero casi las mismas funciones; Power cuesta 20 $ al mes con 500 millones de tokens por semana; Maximum 100 $ al mes con 3.000 millones por semana; los planes de pago sobre todo amplían el uso y se prueban en EE. items.author: 0xAIGOAT
items.text:
Holy sh*t... Elon's xAI built Grok Bot, and one 11-line rulebook turns it into a 7-bot team that launches ideas from X while your laptop is closed 🤯

Meanwhile most people still run hourly bots that burn 1,176 runs a week asking "anything new?"

Scout, Pain Miner, Judge, Builder, Pitch, Inbox, even a Buyer with a $40 cap. One job each, and Chief reads the ledger so you don't have to

-> Monday 09:00: Scout scans X. The only clock
-> Judge scores the idea 0-8: GO or KILL
-> Builder opens ONE pull request and never merges
-> Pitch makes the deck, the launch post and the video
-> Buyer asks before every single payment

1 clock, 6 triggers, about 60 runs a week by the author's math. No cap. Well, one cap: $40 💸

Watch 0:09  when 60 lands next to 1,176.

By Friday the idea is dead with a written reason, or live with a domain, a deck and its first users. Your whole job is approving the money and the posts.

Run it today, not tomorrow. Prompts in the replies, full guide below ↓

items.author: gippp69
items.text:
While I was wiring 7 Grok Bot bots into one launch team, I found the f*cking dumb mistake almost every bot setup makes...

Your bots wake up on a clock, ask "anything new?", get nothing back and burn a run. Every hour. All week.

Here's what else I found and the 5 fixes I use now:

What I found:

• 7 bots on an hourly clock is 1,176 runs a week by my math, and most of them come back empty

• Bots that hand off through email leave you a pile of drafts, because every send waits for your approval

• A "test run" is not a test. It does the real work, so one wrong prompt can act for real

• One greedy bot can eat your whole X budget: 1,000 reads a day, 30 a minute, shared by everyone

• One launch hour with 250 signups on a single email alias breaks the 200 runs an hour cap

• And much more...

It's not just my setup:

- A single bot on a 5 minute clock is 2,016 runs a week, even if nothing ever happens (by my math)
- My launch team does the same job in about 60

How to fix yours:

1. Paste the prompt from the replies into Grok Bot
2. Keep 1 clock (Monday 09:00) and turn everything else into triggers: a bot starts only when the one before it writes DONE
3. Hand off through a shared LEDGER file, never email
4. Give every bot its own X reads budget and a hard STOP at the cap
5. Let only one bot touch money, with a $40 cap and your yes on every single buy

Do it before your next routine fires. Then read the full guide on all 7 bots below ↓

zh-CN.title: 7 个 Grok Bot 组队时发现的空跑问题和 5 个修法
zh-CN.summary: 作者把 7 个 Grok Bot 接成发布小队时发现：按小时定时唤醒的 bot 大多空跑，按作者估算每周 1,176 次；靠邮件交接会堆满待批草稿；测试运行会真的执行；一个 bot 就可能吃光每天 1,000 次、每分钟 30 次的 X 读取额度。作者的修法是只保留周一 9 点一个定时、其余改为上一步写 DONE 才触发、用共享 LEDGER 文件交接、给每个 bot 设 X 读取上限，并只让一个 bot 碰钱，上限 40 美元且每次都要作者批准。

zh-TW.title: 7 個 Grok Bot 組隊時發現的空轉問題與 5 個修法
zh-TW.summary: 作者把 7 個 Grok Bot 接成發布小隊時發現：按小時定時喚醒的 bot 多半空轉，依作者估算每週 1,176 次；靠郵件交接會堆滿待批草稿；測試執行會真的動作；一個 bot 就可能吃光每天 1,000 次、每分鐘 30 次的 X 讀取額度。作者的修法是只保留週一 9 點一個排程、其餘改為上一步寫 DONE 才觸發、用共享 LEDGER 檔交接、為每個 bot 設 X 讀取上限，並只讓一個 bot 碰錢，上限 40 美元且每次都需作者核准。

en.title: Empty runs found while wiring 7 Grok Bot bots, and 5 fixes
en.summary: Wiring 7 Grok Bot bots into a launch team, the author found hourly clocks mostly come back empty (1,176 runs a week by their math), email hand-offs pile up drafts awaiting approval, a test run does real work, and one bot can eat the shared X budget of 1,000 reads a day and 30 a minute. Their fixes: keep one clock (Monday 09:00) and make the rest triggers that fire when the previous bot writes DONE, hand off through a shared LEDGER file, give each bot its own X read cap, and let only one bot touch money with a $40 cap and approval on every buy.

ja.title: Grok Botを7体つないで見つけた空振り実行と5つの対策
ja.summary: 7体のGrok Botをローンチチームにつないだ投稿者は、毎時起動のbotはほぼ空振り（本人の計算で週1,176回）、メールでの受け渡しは承認待ちの下書きが溜まる、テスト実行は本当に動く、1体でXの読み取り枠（1日1,000回・毎分30回）を使い切りうる、と気づいた。対策は、定時は月曜9時の1つだけにし、他は前のbotがDONEを書いたら起動するトリガーにする、共有LEDGERファイルで受け渡す、botごとにX読み取り上限を設ける、お金を扱うのは1体だけで上限40ドル・毎回承認、というもの。

ko.title: Grok Bot 7개를 엮으며 발견한 헛실행과 5가지 해결책
ko.summary: 작성자는 Grok Bot 7개를 런칭 팀으로 연결하면서 매시간 깨우는 bot은 대부분 빈손으로 돌아오고(본인 계산으로 주 1,176회), 이메일로 넘기면 승인 대기 초안이 쌓이며, 테스트 실행도 실제로 동작하고, bot 하나가 하루 1,000회·분당 30회의 X 읽기 한도를 다 쓸 수 있다는 걸 발견했다. 해결책은 정해진 시각은 월요일 9시 하나만 두고 나머지는 이전 bot이 DONE을 쓰면 시작하는 트리거로 바꾸기, 공유 LEDGER 파일로 넘기기, bot마다 X 읽기 한도 두기, 돈은 한 bot만 다루고 40달러 상한에 매번 승인받기다.

ms.title: Larian kosong ditemui semasa menyambung 7 bot Grok Bot, dan 5 pembaikan
ms.summary: Semasa menyambung 7 bot Grok Bot menjadi pasukan pelancaran, penulis mendapati jam setiap jam kebanyakannya kosong (1,176 larian seminggu mengikut kiraannya), serahan melalui e-mel menimbun draf menunggu kelulusan, larian ujian melakukan kerja sebenar, dan satu bot boleh menghabiskan bajet X 1,000 bacaan sehari dan 30 seminit. Pembaikannya: satu jam sahaja (Isnin 09:00) dan selebihnya pencetus apabila bot sebelumnya menulis DONE, serahan melalui fail LEDGER kongsi, had bacaan X bagi setiap bot, dan hanya satu bot menyentuh wang dengan had $40 serta kelulusan setiap pembelian.

vi.title: Lượt chạy rỗng khi nối 7 bot Grok Bot và 5 cách sửa
vi.summary: Khi nối 7 bot Grok Bot thành đội ra mắt, tác giả thấy bot đánh thức theo giờ phần lớn chạy rỗng (theo tính toán của họ là 1.176 lượt mỗi tuần), bàn giao qua email làm dồn bản nháp chờ duyệt, chạy thử là làm thật, và một bot có thể ăn hết hạn mức X 1.000 lượt đọc mỗi ngày, 30 lượt mỗi phút. Cách sửa: chỉ giữ một lịch (thứ Hai 09:00), còn lại là trigger khi bot trước ghi DONE, bàn giao qua tệp LEDGER chung, đặt giới hạn đọc X cho từng bot, và chỉ một bot được đụng tới tiền với trần 40 USD, mỗi lần mua đều cần duyệt.

fr.title: Exécutions à vide repérées en reliant 7 bots Grok Bot, et 5 correctifs
fr.summary: En reliant 7 bots Grok Bot en équipe de lancement, l'auteur a vu que les réveils horaires reviennent surtout vides (1 176 exécutions par semaine selon son calcul), que les relais par e-mail empilent des brouillons à approuver, qu'un test fait le vrai travail et qu'un bot peut épuiser le quota X partagé de 1 000 lectures par jour et 30 par minute. Correctifs : une seule horloge (lundi 9 h) et des déclencheurs quand le bot précédent écrit DONE, relais via un fichier LEDGER partagé, un plafond de lectures X par bot, et un seul bot qui touche à l'argent, plafonné à 40 $ avec validation de chaque achat.

es.title: Ejecuciones vacías al conectar 7 bots de Grok Bot, y 5 arreglos
es.summary: Al conectar 7 bots de Grok Bot en un equipo de lanzamiento, el autor vio que los relojes cada hora vuelven casi siempre vacíos (1.176 ejecuciones a la semana según su cálculo), que pasar trabajo por email acumula borradores por aprobar, que una prueba hace trabajo real y que un bot puede agotar el cupo de X de 1.000 lecturas al día y 30 por minuto. Arreglos: un solo reloj (lunes 09:00) y el resto disparadores cuando el bot anterior escribe DONE, traspasos por un archivo LEDGER compartido, tope de lecturas de X por bot y un único bot que toca dinero, con tope de 40 $ y aprobación en cada compra.

de.title: Leerläufe beim Verbinden von 7 Grok-Bot-Bots und 5 Fixes
de.summary: Beim Verbinden von 7 Grok-Bot-Bots zu einem Launch-Team stellte der Autor fest: Stündliche Weckzeiten laufen meist leer (nach eigener Rechnung 1.176 Läufe pro Woche), Übergaben per E-Mail stapeln Entwürfe zur Freigabe, ein Testlauf erledigt echte Arbeit, und ein Bot kann das geteilte X-Budget von 1.000 Reads am Tag und 30 pro Minute aufbrauchen. Die Fixes: nur ein Zeitplan (Montag 9 Uhr), sonst Trigger, sobald der vorige Bot DONE schreibt, Übergabe über eine gemeinsame LEDGER-Datei, ein X-Read-Limit pro Bot und nur ein Bot mit Geldzugriff, gedeckelt auf 40 $ und mit Freigabe jedes Kaufs.

items.author: gippp69
items.text:
Full prompt ↓ Copy all of it into Grok Bot

Set up my launch team in Grok Bot: 7 bots, 1 clock. An idea shows up on X on Monday. By Friday it is dead with a written reason, or live with a domain, a deck and first users. I only approve money and posts. Target: about 60 runs a week by my math, not 1,176 from 7 hourly bots. Create the bots one by one and show me each prompt before you save it.

RULES
• Work only in /workspace/launch/, one folder per idea. Bots hand off through files, never email.
• Every bot reads the LEDGER file first and starts only when the step before it is DONE. Then it adds: time | bot | DONE | file | next bot. Stuck: BLOCKED plus reason, message me.
• Log every X search in the X reads file, run the budget script first. STOP means stop. Limit: 1,000 X reads a day, 30 a minute.
• Facts get a source link, guesses get GUESS. Never invent numbers, quotes or users.
• Never post, send, buy, pay or delete without my approval. Posts stay drafts. If I deny a card, drop it.

THE 7 BOTS
1. Chief (primary): never does the work. Keeps a "Launch Board" Page. 08:30 brief only if the LEDGER changed.
2. Scout (the only clock): Monday 09:00 or "run scout". Searches X (max 400 reads) for "just launched", "wish there was", "why is there no", plus GitHub Trending, Show HN, Product Hunt. Top 15 table, sends me the top 3.
3. Pain Miner (on Scout DONE): public complaints for the top 5 (max 300 reads), mentions x intensity, 3 source links each.
4. Judge (on Pain Miner DONE): real pain, one 10x number, 7 day v1, first 50 users, 0 to 2 each. 7+ GO, 5 to 6 HOLD, 0 to 4 KILL with one line why.
5. Builder (on GO plus my "build"): SPEC, v1 with tests, ONE pull request, fixes failed checks until merge. I merge.
6. Pitch (on Builder DONE): 7 slide deck, X post, 5 post thread, 30 second video script, 3 reply drafts. Drafts only.
7. Buyer (on Builder DONE or my "buy"): domain, hosting or one API key. Cap $40 per idea, $100 a month. 3 options with renewal price, I approve each one. No auto-renew trials.

1 CLOCK, 6 TRIGGERS
Clock: Monday 09:00 Scout.
Triggers: Scout DONE starts Pain Miner • Pain Miner DONE starts Judge • the pull request starts Builder fixes • mail to a +alias starts Inbox • an @bot tag on X adds to the queue • mail to +meme starts the watch-only Meme Radar.
No other scheduled routines.

FINISH
Confirm the guards. Report the bots, the clock, the triggers and the run estimate by my math (about 60 a week vs 1,176). A test run does real work, so test on a copy. Run Scout once by hand, then wait for my approval.

Skills and routines: https://t.co/hq8v4Mskxb

zh-CN.summary: 作者公开了可直接粘贴进 Grok Bot 的完整提示词：在 /workspace/launch/ 里按想法分文件夹工作，bot 之间只用文件交接，每个 bot 先读 LEDGER，上一步 DONE 才开始；记录每次 X 搜索并遵守每天 1,000、每分钟 30 次的上限；事实附来源，猜测标 GUESS；未经批准不发帖、不发信、不付款、不删除。7 个 bot 分别是 Chief、Scout（唯一定时，周一 9 点）、Pain Miner、Judge（按 0 到 8 分判 GO、HOLD 或 KILL）、Builder（只开一个 PR，由作者合并）、Pitch（只出草稿）和 Buyer（每个想法上限 40 美元、每月 100 美元，每笔需批准）。

zh-TW.title: Grok Bot 發布小隊完整提示詞：7 個 bot、1 個排程
zh-TW.summary: 作者公開了可直接貼進 Grok Bot 的完整提示詞：在 /workspace/launch/ 內依想法分資料夾工作，bot 之間只用檔案交接，每個 bot 先讀 LEDGER，上一步 DONE 才開始；記錄每次 X 搜尋並遵守每天 1,000、每分鐘 30 次的上限；事實附來源，猜測標 GUESS；未經核准不發文、不寄信、不付款、不刪除。7 個 bot 為 Chief、Scout（唯一排程，週一 9 點）、Pain Miner、Judge（以 0 到 8 分判 GO、HOLD 或 KILL）、Builder（只開一個 PR，由作者合併）、Pitch（只出草稿）與 Buyer（每個想法上限 40 美元、每月 100 美元，每筆需核准）。

en.title: Full Grok Bot launch-team prompt: 7 bots, 1 clock
en.summary: The author shares the full prompt to paste into Grok Bot: work only in /workspace/launch/ with one folder per idea, hand off through files, have every bot read the LEDGER first and start only when the previous step is DONE, log every X search within 1,000 reads a day and 30 a minute, link facts and mark guesses GUESS, and never post, send, buy, pay or delete without approval. The 7 bots are Chief, Scout (the only clock, Monday 09:00), Pain Miner, Judge (scores 0 to 8 as GO, HOLD or KILL), Builder (one pull request, the author merges), Pitch (drafts only) and Buyer ($40 per idea, $100 a month, each purchase approved).

ja.title: Grok Botローンチチームの完全プロンプト：bot 7体・定時1つ
ja.summary: 投稿者はGrok Botに貼るだけの完全プロンプトを公開した。/workspace/launch/内でアイデアごとにフォルダを分け、bot同士はファイルで受け渡し、各botはまずLEDGERを読み前の工程がDONEのときだけ始める。X検索はすべて記録し1日1,000回・毎分30回を守る。事実には出典、推測にはGUESSを付け、承認なしに投稿・送信・購入・支払い・削除はしない。7体はChief、Scout（唯一の定時、月曜9時）、Pain Miner、Judge（0〜8点でGO・HOLD・KILL）、Builder（PRは1本、マージは本人）、Pitch（下書きのみ）、Buyer（1アイデア40ドル・月100ドル上限、毎回承認）。

ko.title: Grok Bot 런칭 팀 전체 프롬프트: bot 7개, 정해진 시각 1개
ko.summary: 작성자는 Grok Bot에 그대로 붙여 넣는 전체 프롬프트를 공개했다. /workspace/launch/에서 아이디어별 폴더로 작업하고, bot끼리는 파일로만 넘기며, 모든 bot은 먼저 LEDGER를 읽고 이전 단계가 DONE일 때만 시작한다. X 검색은 모두 기록하고 하루 1,000회·분당 30회를 지킨다. 사실엔 출처를, 추측엔 GUESS를 달고, 승인 없이 게시·발송·구매·결제·삭제를 하지 않는다. 7개 bot은 Chief, Scout(유일한 정시 실행, 월요일 9시), Pain Miner, Judge(0~8점으로 GO·HOLD·KILL), Builder(PR 하나, 병합은 본인), Pitch(초안만), Buyer(아이디어당 40달러·월 100달러 상한, 건마다 승인)다.

ms.title: Prompt penuh pasukan pelancaran Grok Bot: 7 bot, 1 jam
ms.summary: Penulis berkongsi prompt penuh untuk ditampal ke Grok Bot: bekerja hanya dalam /workspace/launch/ dengan satu folder setiap idea, serahan melalui fail, setiap bot membaca LEDGER dahulu dan bermula hanya apabila langkah sebelumnya DONE, catat setiap carian X dalam had 1,000 bacaan sehari dan 30 seminit, pautkan fakta dan tanda tekaan sebagai GUESS, dan jangan siar, hantar, beli, bayar atau padam tanpa kelulusan. 7 bot ialah Chief, Scout (satu-satunya jam, Isnin 09:00), Pain Miner, Judge (skor 0 hingga 8: GO, HOLD atau KILL), Builder (satu pull request, penulis yang gabung), Pitch (draf sahaja) dan Buyer ($40 setiap idea, $100 sebulan, setiap pembelian diluluskan).

vi.title: Prompt đầy đủ cho đội ra mắt Grok Bot: 7 bot, 1 lịch
vi.summary: Tác giả chia sẻ prompt đầy đủ để dán vào Grok Bot: chỉ làm trong /workspace/launch/, mỗi ý tưởng một thư mục, bàn giao qua tệp, mọi bot đọc LEDGER trước và chỉ bắt đầu khi bước trước là DONE, ghi lại mọi lượt tìm X trong giới hạn 1.000 lượt đọc mỗi ngày và 30 mỗi phút, sự thật kèm nguồn, phỏng đoán ghi GUESS, không đăng, gửi, mua, trả tiền hay xóa khi chưa được duyệt. 7 bot gồm Chief, Scout (lịch duy nhất, thứ Hai 09:00), Pain Miner, Judge (chấm 0 đến 8: GO, HOLD hoặc KILL), Builder (một pull request, tác giả tự merge), Pitch (chỉ bản nháp) và Buyer (40 USD mỗi ý tưởng, 100 USD mỗi tháng, mỗi lần mua đều duyệt).

fr.title: Prompt complet d'équipe de lancement Grok Bot : 7 bots, 1 horloge
fr.summary: L'auteur partage le prompt complet à coller dans Grok Bot : travailler seulement dans /workspace/launch/ avec un dossier par idée, se passer le relais par fichiers, chaque bot lit d'abord le LEDGER et ne démarre que si l'étape précédente est DONE, journaliser chaque recherche X dans la limite de 1 000 lectures par jour et 30 par minute, sourcer les faits et marquer les suppositions GUESS, et ne jamais publier, envoyer, acheter, payer ou supprimer sans accord. Les 7 bots : Chief, Scout (seule horloge, lundi 9 h), Pain Miner, Judge (note de 0 à 8 : GO, HOLD ou KILL), Builder (une seule pull request, fusionnée par l'auteur), Pitch (brouillons uniquement) et Buyer (40 $ par idée, 100 $ par mois, chaque achat validé).

es.title: Prompt completo del equipo de lanzamiento en Grok Bot: 7 bots, 1 reloj
es.summary: El autor comparte el prompt completo para pegar en Grok Bot: trabajar solo en /workspace/launch/ con una carpeta por idea, traspasos por archivos, cada bot lee primero el LEDGER y solo empieza si el paso anterior está en DONE, registrar cada búsqueda en X dentro de 1.000 lecturas al día y 30 por minuto, citar fuente en los hechos y marcar GUESS las suposiciones, y nunca publicar, enviar, comprar, pagar ni borrar sin aprobación. Los 7 bots son Chief, Scout (el único reloj, lunes 09:00), Pain Miner, Judge (puntúa de 0 a 8: GO, HOLD o KILL), Builder (un solo pull request, que fusiona el autor), Pitch (solo borradores) y Buyer (40 $ por idea, 100 $ al mes, cada compra aprobada).

de.title: Vollständiger Grok-Bot-Prompt fürs Launch-Team: 7 Bots, 1 Zeitplan
de.summary: Der Autor teilt den kompletten Prompt zum Einfügen in Grok Bot: nur in /workspace/launch/ arbeiten, ein Ordner pro Idee, Übergaben über Dateien, jeder Bot liest zuerst das LEDGER und startet erst, wenn der vorige Schritt DONE ist, jede X-Suche protokollieren bei maximal 1.000 Reads am Tag und 30 pro Minute, Fakten mit Quelle, Vermutungen als GUESS, und nichts posten, senden, kaufen, bezahlen oder löschen ohne Freigabe. Die 7 Bots: Chief, Scout (einziger Zeitplan, Montag 9 Uhr), Pain Miner, Judge (0 bis 8 Punkte: GO, HOLD oder KILL), Builder (ein Pull Request, gemergt vom Autor), Pitch (nur Entwürfe) und Buyer (40 $ pro Idee, 100 $ im Monat, jeder Kauf freigegeben).

items.author: femke_plantinga
items.text:
What do ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet actually do all day?

These 6 terms explain how personal agents keep working while you’re offline.

Every big lab has one now: Grok Bot from xAI, Muse from Meta, Dots from OpenAI and, last week, Duet from Anthropic.

Take one example of an agent that reads your inbox overnight and has a brief ready when you open your laptop.

/1 Own computer
The agent gets its own machine in the cloud, with a browser and apps, so it keeps going after you close your laptop. Dots, Grok Bot and Muse each run on one.

/2 Integrations
This is how it reaches your inbox, your calendar and your Slack. Dots connects to 4,000+ apps, and Muse uses integrations to book, shop and pay.

/3 Memory
What it keeps between tasks: who your manager is, which threads you always ignore, what you asked yesterday. Without it, every morning brief starts from zero.

/4 Routines
What starts the work without you asking: a set time, a new email or a Slack mention. Duet's morning brief is a routine.

/5 Approval gates
The moments it has to stop and ask you first. Duet asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything.

/6 Audit log
A record of every action it took, so you can see what happened while you were away. OpenBot, one of the open-source clones, runs every action through a policy check and logs it.

What I haven't seen any launch fully explain yet is:
What happens when a task gets cut off halfway? 
Does it pick up again without sending the same email twice? 
And does your yes on one task carry over to the next? 

Even Anthropic says Duet can still misjudge what's urgent, so I'd test these before connecting an inbox.

Which of these would you want to see before you give an agent your inbox? 👀

zh-CN.title: 看懂常驻个人代理的 6 个概念
zh-CN.summary: 作者以“夜里读完收件箱、早上备好简报”的代理为例，解释 Dots、Grok Bot、Muse 和 Claude Duet 这类个人代理的 6 个概念：自有云电脑（关电脑后继续运行）、集成（Dots 接 4,000 多个应用）、记忆、routine（定时、新邮件或 Slack 提及触发）、审批关口（Duet 在发送、付款、签署、删除前会询问）以及审计日志。作者指出发布材料还没讲清任务中断后能否续跑而不重复发信、一次批准是否延续到下一任务，建议接入收件箱前先测这些。

zh-TW.title: 看懂常駐個人代理的 6 個概念
zh-TW.summary: 作者以「夜裡讀完收件匣、早上備好簡報」的代理為例，解釋 Dots、Grok Bot、Muse 與 Claude Duet 這類個人代理的 6 個概念：自有雲端電腦（闔上筆電後繼續執行）、整合（Dots 串接 4,000 多個應用）、記憶、routine（排程、新郵件或 Slack 提及觸發）、審批關卡（Duet 在寄送、付款、簽署、刪除前會詢問）以及稽核紀錄。作者指出發布資料尚未說清任務中斷後能否續跑而不重複寄信、一次核准是否延續到下一任務，建議接入收件匣前先測這些。

en.title: Six terms that explain always-on personal agents
en.summary: Using an agent that reads your inbox overnight and has a brief ready by morning, the author explains six terms behind Dots, Grok Bot, Muse and Claude Duet: its own cloud computer, integrations (Dots connects to 4,000+ apps), memory, routines (a set time, a new email or a Slack mention), approval gates (Duet asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes) and an audit log. They note no launch has fully explained whether a task cut off halfway resumes without sending the same email twice, or whether one approval carries over, and suggest testing that before connecting an inbox.

ja.title: 常時稼働のパーソナルエージェントを理解する6つの用語
ja.summary: 夜のうちに受信箱を読み朝にはブリーフを用意するエージェントを例に、Dots、Grok Bot、Muse、Claude Duetに共通する6つの用語を解説する。専用のクラウドPC、連携（Dotsは4,000以上のアプリに接続）、メモリ、routine（決まった時刻・新着メール・Slackのメンションで起動）、承認ゲート（Duetは送信・支払い・署名・削除の前に確認）、監査ログ。途中で止まったタスクが同じメールを二重送信せずに再開できるか、1回の承認が次のタスクに持ち越されるかはどの発表も説明しておらず、受信箱をつなぐ前に試すよう勧めている。

ko.title: 상시 작동 개인 에이전트를 이해하는 6가지 용어
ko.summary: 밤새 받은편지함을 읽고 아침에 브리핑을 준비해 두는 에이전트를 예로 들어, 작성자는 Dots, Grok Bot, Muse, Claude Duet에 공통된 6가지 용어를 설명한다. 자체 클라우드 컴퓨터, 연동(Dots는 4,000개 이상 앱 연결), 메모리, routine(정해진 시각·새 이메일·Slack 멘션으로 시작), 승인 관문(Duet은 발송·결제·서명·삭제 전에 묻는다), 감사 로그다. 중간에 끊긴 작업이 같은 메일을 두 번 보내지 않고 재개되는지, 한 번의 승인이 다음 작업에 이어지는지는 어느 발표도 충분히 설명하지 않았다며 받은편지함 연결 전에 시험해 보라고 권한다.

ms.title: Enam istilah untuk memahami ejen peribadi yang sentiasa aktif
ms.summary: Dengan contoh ejen yang membaca peti masuk semalaman dan menyediakan ringkasan pada waktu pagi, penulis menerangkan enam istilah di sebalik Dots, Grok Bot, Muse dan Claude Duet: komputer awan sendiri, integrasi (Dots bersambung ke lebih 4,000 aplikasi), memori, routine (masa tetap, e-mel baharu atau sebutan Slack), pintu kelulusan (Duet bertanya sebelum menghantar, membayar, menandatangani atau memadam) dan log audit. Penulis menyatakan belum ada pelancaran yang menjelaskan sama ada tugas yang terputus boleh disambung tanpa menghantar e-mel sama dua kali, atau sama ada satu kelulusan terbawa ke tugas seterusnya, dan mencadangkan ujian itu sebelum menyambung peti masuk.

vi.title: Sáu thuật ngữ để hiểu tác tử cá nhân luôn chạy
vi.summary: Lấy ví dụ một tác tử đọc hộp thư qua đêm và soạn sẵn bản tóm tắt buổi sáng, tác giả giải thích sáu thuật ngữ đứng sau Dots, Grok Bot, Muse và Claude Duet: máy tính đám mây riêng, tích hợp (Dots kết nối hơn 4.000 ứng dụng), bộ nhớ, routine (giờ cố định, email mới hoặc lượt nhắc trên Slack), cổng phê duyệt (Duet hỏi trước khi gửi, trả tiền, ký hoặc xóa) và nhật ký kiểm toán. Tác giả lưu ý chưa có bản ra mắt nào giải thích rõ tác vụ bị ngắt giữa chừng có chạy lại mà không gửi trùng email không, hay một lần đồng ý có áp cho tác vụ sau không, và khuyên thử những điều đó trước khi kết nối hộp thư.

fr.title: Six notions pour comprendre les agents personnels toujours actifs
fr.summary: Avec l'exemple d'un agent qui lit la boîte mail la nuit et prépare un brief pour le matin, l'autrice explique six notions derrière Dots, Grok Bot, Muse et Claude Duet : un ordinateur cloud dédié, les intégrations (Dots se connecte à plus de 4 000 apps), la mémoire, les routines (heure fixe, nouvel e-mail ou mention Slack), les points d'approbation (Duet demande avant d'envoyer, payer, signer ou supprimer) et le journal d'audit. Elle note qu'aucun lancement n'explique encore si une tâche interrompue reprend sans renvoyer le même e-mail, ni si un accord vaut pour la tâche suivante, et conseille de le tester avant de connecter une boîte mail.

es.title: Seis términos para entender los agentes personales siempre activos
es.summary: Con el ejemplo de un agente que lee el correo de noche y deja un resumen listo por la mañana, la autora explica seis términos detrás de Dots, Grok Bot, Muse y Claude Duet: ordenador propio en la nube, integraciones (Dots conecta con más de 4.000 apps), memoria, routines (una hora fija, un email nuevo o una mención en Slack), puntos de aprobación (Duet pregunta antes de enviar, pagar, firmar o borrar) y registro de auditoría. Señala que ningún lanzamiento explica aún si una tarea cortada a medias se reanuda sin enviar dos veces el mismo email, ni si una aprobación vale para la siguiente, y recomienda probarlo antes de conectar el correo.

de.title: Sechs Begriffe, die dauerhaft laufende persönliche Agenten erklären
de.summary: Am Beispiel eines Agenten, der nachts das Postfach liest und morgens ein Briefing bereithält, erklärt die Autorin sechs Begriffe hinter Dots, Grok Bot, Muse und Claude Duet: eigener Cloud-Rechner, Integrationen (Dots verbindet sich mit über 4.000 Apps), Gedächtnis, Routines (feste Uhrzeit, neue E-Mail oder Slack-Erwähnung), Freigabepunkte (Duet fragt vor Senden, Zahlen, Unterschreiben oder Löschen) und Audit-Log. Kein Launch erkläre bisher, ob eine abgebrochene Aufgabe ohne doppelte E-Mail weiterläuft oder ob eine Zustimmung für die nächste Aufgabe gilt; das solle man vor dem Anbinden eines Postfachs testen.

items.author: yasutaketin
items.text:
Meta Museの興味深い利用例（Xユーザー・実例中心） $META

お金・請求まわり
•電話・ネット回線の値引き交渉（実際に電話もかける）：AT&Tを$80→$40、Spectrumを$75→$40、Verizonを$516→$386など。Peter Yang氏は年$800超節約したと報告。
•自動車保険の見直し：$3,500/年節約（同じ補償）、別事例では$500→$335/月に当日切り替え。
•フライト遅延補償：7時間遅延でDeltaから$250クレジットを約5分で取得＋再予約。
•運賃下落監視：予約済みフライトを監視して値下がり時にクレジット取得（$1,000超の例あり）。
•未請求金の発見：州の未請求財産から$1,500超を5分程度で見つけ、申請書類まで作成。
•サブスク監査：メールや明細を見て使っていないものを解約し、月$100超・年$1,200相当の節約例。
旅行・予約
•日本旅行のレストラン予約を全部Museに任せ、箱根のホテルに日本語で交渉して非公開ディナーを確保した例。
•フライト・ホテル・移動・レストランを一気に組む。カレンダー連携で空き時間を見て予約。
生活・その他
•Facebook Marketplaceで出品・交渉・購入者対応。
•「タコスの火曜日」みたいな曖昧な指示からInstacartでカート作成〜決済まで。
•古いメール数万通の整理、返品手続き、HVACメンテ予約など、面倒な事務作業をまとめて処理。
•求人応募を数十件自動化して面接まで進めた例。
•イベント準備（ボランティア登録・メール対応・スケジュール作成）を任せて、当日は行くだけ。

傾向 特に「請求交渉・保険見直し・返金・未請求金」が突出して効果を出しており、Xでも「Museが一番使ってるAIになった」「Claude解約した」といった声が見られます。買い物・予約系も多いですが、Amazonはブロックするなどサイトによる制限もあります。
（多くは自己報告ベースなので、実際の結果はケースバイケースです）

zh-CN.title: X 上 Meta Muse 的真实用法汇总
zh-CN.summary: 帖子汇总了 X 用户自述的 Muse 用例：打电话砍话费和网费（如 AT&T 从 80 美元降到 40 美元，Peter Yang 称一年省下 800 多美元）、重比车险、航班延误 7 小时约 5 分钟拿到 Delta 250 美元补偿、监控已订机票降价、5 分钟左右找到 1,500 多美元州政府待领财产、审查并退订不用的订阅。还有替日本行程订餐厅并用日语与箱根酒店交涉、Facebook Marketplace 买卖、Instacart 下单、批量求职等。作者提醒多为自我报告，有些网站（如 Amazon）会拦截。

zh-TW.title: X 上 Meta Muse 的真實用法彙整
zh-TW.summary: 貼文彙整 X 使用者自述的 Muse 用例：打電話砍話費與網路費（如 AT&T 從 80 美元降到 40 美元，Peter Yang 稱一年省下 800 多美元）、重比車險、航班延誤 7 小時約 5 分鐘拿到 Delta 250 美元補償、監控已訂機票降價、約 5 分鐘找到 1,500 多美元州政府待領財產、檢查並退訂不用的訂閱。還有替日本行程訂餐廳並用日語與箱根飯店交涉、Facebook Marketplace 買賣、Instacart 下單、批次求職等。作者提醒多為自我報告，部分網站（如 Amazon）會封鎖。

en.title: A roundup of real Meta Muse uses seen on X
en.summary: The post collects self-reported Muse uses from X users: calling to cut phone and internet bills (AT&T from $80 to $40; Peter Yang reported saving over $800 a year), re-shopping car insurance, getting a $250 Delta credit in about 5 minutes after a 7-hour delay, watching booked fares for drops, finding over $1,500 in state unclaimed property in about 5 minutes, and auditing unused subscriptions. Others include booking restaurants for a Japan trip and negotiating in Japanese with a Hakone hotel, Facebook Marketplace selling, Instacart orders and bulk job applications. The author notes most are self-reports and some sites such as Amazon block it.

ja.title: Xで見つかったMeta Museの実例まとめ
ja.summary: Xユーザーの自己申告をもとにMuseの使い方をまとめた投稿。電話・ネット回線の値引き交渉（AT&Tを80ドルから40ドルへ、Peter Yang氏は年800ドル超の節約を報告）、自動車保険の見直し、7時間遅延でDeltaから約5分で250ドルのクレジット取得、予約済みフライトの値下がり監視、州の未請求財産1,500ドル超を約5分で発見、未使用サブスクの解約など。日本旅行のレストラン予約や箱根のホテルとの日本語交渉、Facebook Marketplaceでの売買、Instacartの注文、求人応募の自動化もある。多くは自己報告で、Amazonのようにブロックするサイトもあると注意している。

ko.title: X에서 본 Meta Muse 실제 활용 사례 모음
